title: Require priority-export routes at Tauri startup
summary: Add the backend-owned priority-export read and command routes to the Tauri startup contract gate.
reason: Remediate P2 AUDIT-FIND-W09-013. The Python Local API contract and handlers expose both priority-export routes, but the native shell could accept a backend missing that live feature.
behavior_before: Tauri startup required queue priority and strategy routes but omitted GET and POST /api/queue/priority-export, so startup validation did not prove the backend supported the complete queue export feature.
behavior_after: Tauri startup requires authenticated GET and POST /api/queue/priority-export, and the existing exact Rust-versus-Python contract test prevents future method/path/auth drift.
tests_added: The existing Tauri scaffold exact-set assertion now covers both priority-export method rows against the canonical Python Local API contract.
manual_validation: Exact Tauri-versus-Python Local API route-set assertion plus priority-export service tests passed: 20 tests and 19 subtests.
Full Tauri shell scaffold passed: 96 tests; the prior AUDIT-FIND-W09-013 baseline is removed.
cargo fmt --check and cargo check --release --locked passed.
Project index/dependency graph and feature file map checks passed.
Summary-integrity, feature-card, and risky-registry tooling passed: 30 tests and 70 subtests.
Risky-file registry and architecture guardrails passed; god-file guard reported the unchanged baseline of 0 errors and 51 warnings.
Global summary freshness reported only the same six pre-existing stale files outside this packet.
validate_changes --require-worktree-coverage passed with 1,150 valid packets before completion.
rollback_plan: Revert the two required-route rows, generated summary/maps, and this packet together. Do not remove the startup requirements unless the backend feature and canonical route inventory are intentionally removed in the same change.
notes: This batch changes only native startup compatibility validation. The backend retains strict empty-object request validation and owns priority-export persistence and queue policy. No media, queue export, launch, or filesystem mutation is executed, so representative real-media validation is not required.
